reasoning: Partition the closed unit square [0,1]^2 into four closed congruent subsquares of side 1/2 (split at x=1/2 and y=1/2). Each point of the square lies in at least one subsquare. With 5 points and 4 subsquares, the pigeonhole principle gives two points in the same subsquare. The maximum distance between two points of a closed square of side 1/2 is its diagonal, sqrt((1/2)^2 + (1/2)^2) = sqrt(1/2) = sqrt(2)/2. Hence those two points are at distance at most sqrt(2)/2.
